parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a cranium split by a deep stitched crease down the middle, swollen lobes either side, pink flesh-toned clay skin, a greasy black comb-over, raised grey clay wrinkle ridges on the forehead. His huge oversized bobble head is entirely covered by a filthy lumpy burlap sack pulled all the way down over the whole skull and face, ragged cut eye holes, a cross-stitched mouth, rope tied tight at the neck; no skin or hair visible. The sack is pulled fully DOWN over the face with its eye holes right over his eyes, never pushed up on top of the head like a cap and never covering only half the face; on a pointed cone skull the sack covers the whole cone too. Wearing a slate-blue clay work jacket with a brown leather collar, stitched leather patches and a grey knit undershirt, a worn leather tool belt with rusty tools and pouches, his right fist grips a rusty hatchet with a pitted, chipped blade smeared with blood; his LEFT fist tightly grips a rusty woodcutter axe by its long wooden handle, the axe resting up on his left shoulder with the blade behind his shoulder, carried in his hand, not strapped to his back. A bright neon chartreuse-green (hex #CCFF00) pressed-clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands are full and both are tight clenched fists, knuckles toward the camera: the right fist grips the held weapon, the left fist grips the second weapon by its handle as described. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora

The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a huge tall lumpy dome skull with dents and bumps, like the master reference, sallow yellowish clay skin, completely bald. A patchwork mask of stitched burlap and riveted scrap-metal plates, exactly two round brass goggles with red lenses sitting directly over his two eyes (the eyes seen through the lenses, nothing else on the nose or snout), a wire-stitched mouth, a leather strap with a buckle over the crown. Wearing a grimy plaid flannel shirt, a worn leather tool belt with rusty tools and pouches, he wields a LONG-HANDLED garden string trimmer (weed whacker) in BOTH hands, fitted with a blood-smeared round toothed circular saw blade instead of trimmer line. It is a long thin straight rusty steel pole, longer than his arm: at the near end a grimy motor housing with a pistol trigger grip held in his right fist, a black D-shaped loop handle clamped halfway along the pole held in his left fist, and at the far end of the pole a small scuffed guard over the saw disc. It is NOT a hand-held circular saw or angle grinder; no backpack, no brand name, no lettering. A swamp-green pressed-clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands hold the weed whacker, one fist on the rear trigger grip and the other on the loop handle; the shaft angled up across his body so the saw blade is raised beside his head, the whole tool inside the frame; neither hand hangs empty.
